**ElevenLabs voices for read-aloud.**

- Does the system voice sound robotic? Add your ElevenLabs API key in **Settings → Device & permissions → Read-aloud voice**. Replies, the 🔊 Read aloud button and Voice chat then use natural ElevenLabs voices.
- Pick a voice from your account and a model (Flash v2.5 is fast and cheap, Multilingual v2 is most natural), then tap *Preview*.
- The key stays in the phone's gateway. If credits run out or there's no internet, it falls back to the system voice.

New: **talk by voice.**

- **Tap 🎤** to speak; your words appear in the input box as you talk.
- **Long-press 🎤 for hands-free Voice chat**: speak → sent automatically → Claude's answer is read aloud → the mic turns on again. Tap the circle to interrupt.
- **🔊 Read aloud** under every Claude reply.
- Uses the phone's built-in speech recognition and text-to-speech, in your interface language.

**Ask Aure now works with WhatsApp too.**

- WhatsApp messages don't use Android's text menu, so: **long-press the message → Copy**, then open Ask Aure from the **Quick Settings tile** (pull down the shade) or the **app icon shortcut** (long-press Aure Code → *Ask copied text*).
- **Share → Ask Aure** is available in apps that can share text.
- Nothing copied? Type your question straight into the panel.

New: **Ask Aure from any app.**

- Select text in WhatsApp, Chrome, a PDF or any other app and pick **Ask Aure** in the text menu. The Aure panel opens over that app, with no app switching.
- One tap to **Explain, Translate, Summarize, Improve writing, Draft a reply, Explain code or Fix code**. Aure picks the most likely one for you.
- Answers stream in as they're written. **Ask a follow-up**, **Replace text** in the original box, **Copy**, **Share** or **Continue in Aure**.
- Safe: Claude gets no tools in this mode, so text from another app can't make your device do anything.

New icon: an aurora star in a night sky, replacing the `>_` terminal icon.

- The app icon, setup-screen logo, welcome-screen logo and browser tab icon all use the same image.
- While the app is preparing something, the star twinkles slowly (the `_` cursor used to blink).

This update finishes the Indonesian translation and removes what was left of the original app's name.

## What's new

- **Command replies follow your language.** `/model`, `/effort` and `/autocompact` now answer in the interface language.
- **Status messages are translated.** Generation errors, Claude Code update progress, git errors and Repair log entries now follow the interface language.
- **Indonesian terminal scripts.** `priv`, `cc-mem`, `pkg` and `aurecode-selftest` print Indonesian messages.
- **Our own release notes.** The "What's new" window and the Changelog page now show Aure Code notes only.

## Other

- The usage share card is marked "Aure Code".
- The hint for installing the toolkit from a local file now points to the `zesbe/aure-code` releases page.
- Untitled sessions show "(Untitled)" in the interface language.

First release of **Aure Code**: the official Claude Code running natively on Android, now with its own name, look and language.

## What's new

- **New name and look.** The icon, the setup-screen logo and the welcome logo now use the Aure Code identity (an aurora tile with `>_`).
- **Indonesian interface.** Every menu, setting, dialog, notification, the Help page and these release notes are available in Indonesian. Pick it under Settings → Language, or follow the system language.
- **Installs side by side** with the original app: its own package (`cc.codtest`), shared folder `/sdcard/AureCode` and a separate gateway port.
- **Updates install in place.** The version number goes up with every build and the signing key stays the same, so updating never needs an uninstall. An installed developer toolkit is not downloaded again.
- **Its own toolkit.** The developer toolkit is built for Aure Code and downloaded from GitHub `zesbe/aure-code`.

## Other

- The original project's download mirrors and announcements are turned off, since they only fit the original app.
- "Report on GitHub" and the Community page now point to the Aure Code repository.
